name: House of Miller at Millbach

location.text: Millbach, Millcreek Township, Lebanon County, Pennsylvania

dates.altered: 'The interiors of two rooms were removed in 1926 and are installed in Philadelphia Museum of Art' (survey), where they are catalogued as the Mueller House kitchen and a second room. The sash was later changed from six-over-six to Victorian four-over-four.
dates.note: A datestone over the south entrance carries the year and the builders' names. Wikipedia and the mill gazetteer disagree about the mill: 1784 (Wikipedia, and the survey's addendum head) against 1778 (MillPictures.com). Both recorded.

note: The house a fluent reader of this tradition names first, on the federal survey's own judgment: 'one of the finest and best known examples ... of Pennsylvania-German architecture'. It carries the tradition's most legible datestone, in dialect, and its kitchen is a period room in the Philadelphia Museum of Art. TWO THINGS ABOUT THE ROOF, read through bad OCR and worth stating carefully: the roof is a GAMBREL, where the node's prose says 'a steep, forty-five to fifty degree roof'; and the pent roof -- 'Two pent caves cress the gable eno.s', pent eaves crossing the GABLE ENDS -- runs on the ends and not, as the node's prose has it, 'across the facade at the second-floor line'. No dimension is legible in the extracted spans; Downs 1929 carries measured drawings and was not reachable.
